title: Algebraic diagonal Hom and its generator under arbitrary scalar extension
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Put $B=A\otimes_R A$, $p_1(a)=a\otimes1$, and let $A$ be a $B$-module by multiplication. Work in ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. Let $M\in D(A)$ be pseudo-coherent over $A$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] and have finite Tor amplitude over $R$: there exist integers $a\le b$ such that $H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $R$-module $N$ in degree zero and $i\notin[a,b]$. Set $M_1=M\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}B$. Assume $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A[0],M_1)\cong A[0]$ in $D(B)$, and let $\gamma:A[0]\to M_1$ generate the cyclic $A$-module $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(A[0],M_1)$, whose action is by precomposition with multiplication on $A$. For any ring map $R\to R'$, put $A'=A\otimes_RR'$, $B'=A'\otimes_{R'}A'$, $M'=M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$ and $M'_1=M'\otimes_{A',p'_1}^{\mathbf L}B'$. Let $\gamma':A'[0]\to M'_1$ be the image of $\gamma$ under derived extension from $B$ to $B'$, using the canonical identifications $A\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\simeq A'$ and $M_1\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\simeq M'_1$. Then $R\operatorname{Hom}_{B'}(A'[0],M'_1)\cong A'[0]$ in $D(B')$, and $\gamma'$ generates the cyclic $A'$-module $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B')}(A'[0],M'_1)$. No flatness of $R\to R'$ or Noetherianity is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing, part (2) and its final generator assertion; hypotheses expanded from Tag 0E2C, definition-relative-dualizing-complex. Only the diagonal-Hom and generator conclusions are taken here; existence of a complex is not asserted.

proof.text: Use temporary notation $r:D\to C$ for a flat finitely presented ring map and $C_T=C\otimes_DT$, $Q=C\otimes_DC$, $Q_T=C_T\otimes_TC_T$. Flat module base change makes $Q$ flat over $D$ and its coprojections flat over $C$. The Tor-independent tensor comparison of lem-sfb-perfect-coinduction-tor-independent-exchange, with base ring $D$, algebra $Q$ and extension $T$, identifies $N\otimes_Q^{\mathbf L}Q_T$ with $N\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}T$. For $N=C[0]$ this is $C_T[0]$, since $C$ is $D$-flat. For $N=U\otimes_{C,p_1}^{\mathbf L}Q$, associativity identifies it with $(U\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}C_T)\otimes_{C_T,p_{1,T}}^{\mathbf L}Q_T$. These are the specified diagonal and target identifications; the tensor comparison respects derived morphisms and iteration.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, tensor-transitivity and diagonal base-change paragraph; more-algebra.tex Tag 0E1U, proof (b).

proof.text: We will also use relative perfection after extension and after the coprojection. A pseudo-coherent $U$ has a bounded-above finite-free $C$ representative by definition. It is K-flat, so scalar extension gives a bounded-above finite-free representative over $C_T$. For a $D$-perfect $U$, the new Hom-model lemma applied over $D\to C$ with source $C[0]$ and target $U$ supplies a bounded $D$-flat representative $F$. Its termwise tensor with $T$ represents $U\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}C_T$, by that lemma's construction, and is bounded and $T$-flat by flat module base change. Tensoring with any $T$-module therefore stays in its fixed bounded interval. For $U_1=U\otimes_{C,p_1}^{\mathbf L}Q$, the finite-free representative extends along the flat coprojection and remains finite-free over $Q$; a bounded $D$-flat representative is $F\otimes_D C$. Indeed $F\otimes_{C,p_1}Q=F\otimes_D C$, and the second factor $C$ is $D$-flat. Thus $U_1$ is pseudo-coherent over $Q$ and has finite Tor amplitude over $D$.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, relative-perfection and Hom-model prerequisites; more-algebra.tex Tag 0DHW, lemma-base-change-relatively-perfect.

proof.text: First suppose $D$ is Noetherian. Choose a finite polynomial presentation $P=D[x_1,\ldots,x_e]\twoheadrightarrow C$ and put $V=r^!D=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(C,P)[e]$. The algebraic shriek calculus gives this model; the relative-perfection theorem says that $V$ is $D$-perfect. The rings $C,Q$ are Noetherian by the finite-type algebra theorem. Flat base change in the shriek calculus along $D\to C$, using the second coprojection $p_2:C\to Q$, gives $V_1\cong p_2^!C$. For multiplication $\delta:Q\to C$, the surjective-map clause identifies $R\operatorname{Hom}_Q(C,V_1)$ with the restriction of $\delta^!V_1$. Composition gives $\delta^!p_2^!C\cong(\delta\circ p_2)^!C\cong C$ (on ring maps, $\delta\circ p_2=1_C$). Hence the diagonal Hom is $C[0]$ in $D(Q)$. Composition is applicable because its input $C[0]$ is bounded below. This argument works for every Noetherian flat finitely presented algebra, without a complete-intersection assumption.

source.place: Tag 0E2E, lemma-relative-dualizing-noetherian, entire proof; Tag 0E2F, Noetherian starting complex.

proof.text: Still with $D$ Noetherian, let $D\to T$ have Noetherian target. The polynomial quotient $C$ is perfect over $P$ by lem-trf-flat-polynomial-quotient-perfect. Write $P_T=P\otimes_DT$. Since $P$ and $C$ are flat over $D$, the tensor comparison in Step 1 (using $P$ as the flat algebra) gives $C\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P_T\simeq C_T[0]$. Thus $C$ and $P_T$ are Tor independent over $P$. Apply the perfect coinduction exchange over $P$ to the coefficient $P[e]$: it gives $V\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}C_T\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_{P_T}(C_T,P_T)[e]$. The right side is exactly the polynomial model of Step 3 for $T\to C_T$. It is $T$-perfect and its diagonal Hom is $C_T[0]$. In particular this applies to every residue field $T=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ of $D$. No claim of flatness of $D\to T$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, Noetherian-target case, using Tag 0BZV, lemma-base-change-relative-algebraic; its perfect-resolution calculation is supplied by the cited exchange.

proof.text: For the same Noetherian $D\to C$, form $Q=C\otimes_DC$ and $V_1$ as above. Multiplication $Q\twoheadrightarrow C$ and the flat finitely presented maps from $D$ satisfy lem-sfb-flat-fp-quotient-pseudocoherent. Applying it to $C[0]$ shows that this diagonal object is pseudo-coherent over $Q$. Step 2 gives that $V_1$ is pseudo-coherent over $Q$ and has finite Tor amplitude over $D$. The new Hom-model lemma, now for $D\to Q$ with source $C[0]$ and target $V_1$, supplies a bounded-below complex $E^\bullet$ of $D$-flat finitely presented $Q$-modules. It represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_Q(C,V_1)$; $E\otimes_DT$ represents the corresponding diagonal Hom for every $D\to T$, including arbitrary non-Noetherian $T$. The normalization on degree-zero cocycles is the derived extension of the diagonal class.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, application of more-algebra.tex Tags 0E1T and 0E1U.

proof.text: By Step 3, $H^0(E)\cong C$ as a $Q$-module, and it is $D$-flat. By Step 4 and the Hom model, $H^i(E\otimes_D\kappa(\mathfrak p))=0$ for $i\ne0$ at every prime of $D$. The new fibrewise concentration lemma applies with the Noetherian algebra $Q$ and gives, for every $D\to T$, a specified truncation zigzag $E\otimes_DT\simeq(H^0(E)\otimes_DT)[0]\cong C_T[0]$ in $D(Q_T)$. Its map on zeroth cohomology sends $[z]\otimes t$ to $[z\otimes t]$. By the Hom-model normalization and the Hom/cohomology identification, this is the map on derived diagonal morphisms. In particular the diagonal Hom is $C_T[0]$, and the base change of any generator at $D$ generates at $T$. More generally, for $D\to T\to T'$, the induced map on diagonal morphisms is scalar extension $C_T\to C_{T'}$, because both are obtained from $H^0(E)\otimes_D(-)$ by this same zigzag. This proves the needed assertions for the extensions of the Noetherian model, including their actual maps on classes.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, final two paragraphs and final sentence: universal concentration and generator assertion.

proof.text: Return to the original arbitrary $R\to A$. The flat-subring model theorem supplies a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra $R_0\subset R$ and a flat finitely presented $R_0\to A_0$ with $A_0\otimes_{R_0}R\cong A$. Every ideal of $\mathbf Z$ is zero or generated by its least positive element, so $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian. The finite-type Noetherian theorem then makes $R_0$ and $A_0$ Noetherian. Let $V_0$ be the polynomial complex of Step 3 and put $N=V_0\otimes_{A_0}^{\mathbf L}A$. Steps 2 and 6 say that $N$ is $R$-perfect and has diagonal Hom $A[0]$. The supplied $M$ has precisely those same two properties. The arbitrary-ring uniqueness lemma therefore gives an isomorphism $\alpha:N\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ in $D(A)$. It need not preserve any chosen generator. With $N'=N\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$, Step 6 applied to $R_0\to R'$ gives the diagonal Hom of $N'$ as $A'[0]$. Extending $\alpha$ and then along the coprojection gives an isomorphism $N'_1\cong M'_1$. Hence the diagonal Hom of $M'$ is also $A'[0]$ in $D(B')$.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, first paragraph: reduction to a Noetherian model and uniqueness (Tag 0E2D).

proof.text: For the generator assertion put $\eta=\alpha_1^{-1}\circ\gamma$ in $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(A,N_1)$. Postcomposition with $\alpha_1$ is an $A$-linear isomorphism: it commutes with precomposition by multiplication on $A$. Thus $\eta$ generates. Step 6 for the composable maps $R_0\to R\to R'$ identifies the extension of this Hom module with its scalar extension from $A$ to $A'$, including the map on classes. Tensoring the surjection $A\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(A,N_1)$, $a\mapsto\eta\circ m_a$, gives the surjection (each pure tensor has a preimage, so surjectivity is preserved) $A'\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B')}(A',N'_1)$, $a'\mapsto\eta'\circ m_{a'}$. Hence $\eta'$ generates. Functoriality of extension gives $\gamma'=\alpha'_1\circ\eta'$; the same precomposition calculation makes postcomposition by $\alpha'_1$ an $A'$-linear isomorphism. Consequently $\gamma'$ generates as asserted. The argument also covers $A'=0$, when both modules are zero.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, final generator assertion; explicit transfer from the Noetherian model by naturality of the Hom-complex construction.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0E2F, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing, proof of (2) and generator assertion; Noetherian polynomial calculation expanded using Tags 0E2E and 0BZV.
